key_insight: Real-world sensitivity of an FDA-cleared pulmonary embolism AI triage tool was 64.1%, versus 93% in its clearance summary, and varied by site, embolus location, and time.
clinical_relevance: Lower detection of peripheral and chronic emboli highlights why aggregate performance may obscure clinically relevant gaps in deployed AI triage.
method: Retrospective evaluation of 14,736 CT pulmonary angiography examinations across six sites, July 2023–March 2026.
Report-derived reference labels used an LLM pipeline validated against 600 radiologist-annotated reports (κ = 0.98).
Assessed subgroup and site performance, plus temporal trends using logistic and segmented regression.
evidence_signal: Among 1,402 PE-positive examinations, sensitivity was 64.1% (95% CI, 61.5–66.6%) and specificity was 98.8% (98.6–99.0%); sensitivity differed by 13 percentage points between the two highest-volume sites.
watch_item: This retrospective, single-health-system study cannot establish whether temporal changes reflected data drift or undocumented model or threshold changes; independent monitoring remains important.
paper_title: Silent Drift and Site-level Variance in Clinical AI: Real-world performance and subgroup analysis for post-market monitoring of an FDA-cleared artificial intelligence (AI) triage tool for high-risk use case of pulmonary embolism
